predecessors.name: Kingdom of Poland
predecessors.text: the Sandomierz Province (eastern Lesser Poland, centred on Sandomierz), given to Henry of Sandomierz by Bolesław III's testament

successors.name: Kingdom of Poland
successors.text: the whole Sandomierz province, which Władysław I the Elbow-high 'seized' after Wenceslaus II's death in 1305; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape covers Sandomierz from 1305

ledger.x: 1138: Bolesław III's testament takes effect and Henry of Sandomierz receives the Sandomierz Province.
1166: Wiślica splits off as Henry dies.
1173: Casimir II reunites the province.
1177: Casimir II takes the Seniorate at Kraków.
1186: Casimir II takes Masovia.
1195: the war for Kraków begins.
1198: Mieszko III wins Kraków by agreement.
1198: Kraków passes to Mieszko III.
1199: Leszek holds Kraków for a short time.
1199: Mieszko III resumes Kraków.
c. 1200: Konrad takes Masovia and Kuyavia. 'Leszek and Konrad divided their domains. Konrad received Masovia and Kuyavia, and Leszek kept Sandomierz'.
1206: Leszek is High Duke at Kraków.
1210: Mieszko Tanglefoot seizes Kraków.
1211: Leszek recovers Kraków.
1214: peace of Spiš gives Leszek Przemyśl and Lubaczów.
1215: the Hungarians take Przemyśl and Lubaczów back.
1227: Leszek is killed and Kraków leaves Sandomierz.
1235: Konrad of Masovia takes the Radom district.
1239: Konrad gives up on Sandomierz.
1241: Konrad of Masovia enters Kraków while Bolesław V is in exile.
1243: Bolesław V wins Kraków at Suchodoły.
1243: Bolesław V becomes High Duke at Kraków.
1279: Kraków is separated from Sandomierz.
1292: Wenceslaus II of Bohemia takes Sandomierz.
1294: Cliopatria drops the eastern edge of Sandomierz.
1304: Władysław the Elbow-high returns and takes Wiślica.
1304: last year of the Cliopatria shape; the land passes to Łokietek's Poland.

wars.name: War for the Seniorate (Mozgawa)
wars.outcome: Leszek the White and Konrad of Masovia against Mieszko III the Old, who regained the Seniorate Province by agreement with Helen of Znojmo in 1198 and held it (Leszek briefly in 1199) until 13 March 1202.

wars.name: Battle of Zawichost
wars.outcome: On 14 October 1205 Leszek and Konrad defeated Roman the Great, who was killed; no Polish land changed hands.

wars.name: Leszek's war for Galicia (Bobrka, Spiš)
wars.outcome: After Leszek's defeat at the Bobrka River the peace of Spiš gave him Przemyśl and Lubaczów in 1214; the Hungarians took them back in 1215.

wars.name: Wars of Bolesław V with Konrad I of Masovia
wars.outcome: Konrad captured Bolesław in 1233 and took the Radom district in 1235; Bolesław won Kraków at Suchodoły on 25 May 1243, lost and retook Lelów in 1246, and Konrad died on 31 August 1247.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Poland (1241)
wars.outcome: The Mongols took Lublin and Zawichost in January 1241 and burned Sandomierz on 13 February; Bolesław V fled to Hungary and Moravia.

wars.name: Mongol-Ruthenian raid of 1259-1260
wars.outcome: In November 1259 Mongols and Ruthenians destroyed Sandomierz, Lublin and Kraków and left Lesser Poland in February 1260; no annexation.

wars.name: Leo of Galicia's invasion of Lublin and Sandomierz
wars.outcome: Leo invaded Lublin in February 1280, crossed the Vistula and besieged Sandomierz; he fled after the battle of Goźlice on 23 February 1280.

wars.name: War for the Kraków succession
wars.outcome: After Leszek the Black's death (30 September 1288) Władysław the Elbow-high held Sandomierz from 1289; Bohemian troops drove him out in 1292 and Wenceslaus II ruled Sandomierz and Kraków until 1305.

certainty.note: Sandomierz Land is a duchy of castellanies with no treaty or survey lines on the pages opened; its frontiers with Rus' (the San and Bug) and Masovia are approximate.
